newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: FOCUS - EU suspends ministerial meetings with Iran.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU suspends ministerial meetings with Iran.

text.p: The European Union on Tuesday suspended ministerial meetings with Iran in response to a German court ruling that cited Iran's rulers for ordering political assassinations.
The move was seen as a political gesture reflecting the EU's determination to fight terrorism in all its forms.

"This is confirmation of the EU's condemnation of state inspired acts of terrorism. With this show of solidarity the EU is capable of delivering a coordinated follow-up (to withdrawing its ambassadors from Tehran on April 10)," an EU diplomat said.
EU foreign ministers meeting in Luxembourg agreed that ambassadors from the 15 EU nations could return to Tehran if individual countries wanted them to.
"There was consensus that the ambassadors could go back...from today," German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told reporters.

A statement said the EU will continue its arms embargo on Iran, will not grant visas to Iranians with intelligence or security functions and will move to exclude all Iranian intelligence personnel from the European Union.
"Under the present circumstances...there is no basis for the continuation of the critical dialogue between the EU and Iran," it said.
A spokesman for the National Council of Resistance of Iran, which opposes the Tehran government, welcomed the EU stance.
"This position shows that the conscience of the European Union is awakening to the issue of Iranian terrorism. This was a necessary reaction," he told Reuters.
The National Council, he said, hoped that in the long-term the EU would sever all diplomatic ties with Iran and end the critical dialogue on a permanent basis.
The EU's policy of critical dialogue has involved holding talks with Tehran while trying to get Iran to move closer to the West.

The EU ministers said they wanted to have a constructive relationship with Iran, but this was only possible "if the Iranian authorities respect the norms of international law and refrain from acts of terrorism..."
The return of EU ambassadors is seen as a sign that the EU is reluctant to damage its lucrative ties with Iran. The bloc is Iran's biggest trading partner.

The United States has urged the 15-member bloc to take a hard line against Tehran and join economic sanctions Washington has imposed on Iran for alleged sponsorship of international terrorism. Iran denies the charges.
EU governments recalled their envoys for consultations after a Berlin court accused Tehran of ordering the 1992 murder of four Kurdish dissidents in Germany.
Tehran has denied involvement in the murders and expelled four German diplomats from Tehran after Bonn kicked out four Iranian diplomats.

Diplomats noted that the return of ambassadors would help missions monitor Iranian presidential elections on May 23 which will see President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani step down after eight years in office.

Opponents of the Tehran government staged a noisy demonstration outside the building where the ministers were meeting. Organisers said there were 3,000 demonstrators but police estimate it was several hundred. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
